A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FoREST and Spatial-Guided prompting. All 19 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including figures, tables and appendices, support comparison. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM question-answering, FoR-identification, layout-generation and text-to-image results, including additional analyses in Appendices C-E.

after.justification: v2 retains these experimental results and adds model comparisons, attention and template analyses, and a three-participant human study.

M1.justification: SG still extracts directional, topological, distance and FoR information before QA or layout generation, using four crafted examples. Section 4.3 and the corresponding prompt listings retain the same procedure; additional evaluated backbones do not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: v2 adds a small human participant population for studying FoR bias on sampled A-split questions (Section 4.1; Appendix I). The synthetic FoREST data coverage, English language, four FoR classes, object categories and existing QA, identification and T2I tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The QA comparison set expands substantially: Qwen2VL-72B is evaluated under all four prompting settings in Tables 1-2, a human baseline is added for A-split, and o4-mini-high is compared with GPT-4o prompting variants in Tables 16-17. Existing model and diffusion comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a human-study protocol with three participants, 150 questions per participant, 25 questions from each of six case/perspective groups, randomized ordering and no time limit. It also introduces attention-based response grouping, template-wise QA evaluation and high reasoning effort for o4-mini-high. The retained automated QA and T2I settings remain substantively unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses examine Qwen2 attention during successful and failed perspective handling, Qwen2 versus Qwen2VL confusion patterns, illustrated QA bias and reasoning failures, and sensitivity across five question templates (Appendices B-E; Figures 5-11; Table 9). The earlier temperature and FoR-identification analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-model-run uncertainty estimates. v2's participant accuracies, human averages and template ranges add descriptive results without introducing an uncertainty-estimation procedure or changing seed reporting.

E6.justification: Matched original result tables retain their numerical values. Substantial additions include Qwen2VL SG+CoT C-split camera/relatum averages of 75.9%/32.7%, human A-split averages of 85.3%/96.7%, and o4-mini-high C-split averages of 71.4%/84.5%. Template-specific scores and attention/error findings are also newly reported.

T1.justification: The FoR definitions, spatial roles and mathematical notation remain substantively unchanged, with no added theorems, proofs or derivations. The size-aware containment clarification in v2 Section 3.2 restates the container-appropriateness consideration already documented in v1 Appendix B.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: FoREST, identification of FoR-dependent model weaknesses, and SG prompting for QA and text-to-image generation. The additional evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretations involving attention allocation, visual training and viewpoint-biased training data, human FoR preferences, and template sensitivity. It explicitly discusses Qwen2VL's relatum-perspective failures and o4-mini-high's perspective tradeoff, and acknowledges that the human study cannot establish participants' mental scene reconstructions (Appendices B, C, E, I and J).

D1.justification: v2 adds QA count breakdowns, details of GPT template generation and manual validation, and human-study instructions. Hardware reporting changes from one to two A6000 GPUs while retaining approximately 300 GPU hours. Conversely, the specific gpt-4o-2024-11-20 identifier is removed. These are documentation changes, without evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 adds Coventry et al. (2018), Forster et al. (2023) and Wang et al. (2024), supporting human-bias discussion and Qwen2-VL evaluation. Related work is condensed, including removal of the explicit claim of broader FoR coverage than Liu et al. (2023), while the overall benchmark positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits definitions, task descriptions and results discussion, and consolidates dataset statistics and construction details under Appendix A. Appendix headings and cross-references change to accommodate additions, but the main section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with new confusion matrices, attention plots and QA example diagrams in Figures 5-11, expanded QA comparison tables, and new template, human and reasoning-model tables. Dataset statistics and template tables are split into separate displays. Original figures are retained, including v1 Figures 5-6 as v2 Figures 12-13.

improvement.justification: v2 improves empirical scrutiny through additional model and human comparisons, template-sensitivity checks and diagnostic analyses. Table 9 provides useful evidence of SG's reduced sensitivity to wording. The gain is limited by speculative training-based explanations and incomplete integration: RQ2 retains a 55.5% ceiling despite higher new Table 2 results, and Section 8 still denies human-subject involvement despite Appendix I's study.
